title: Flat fixed-coefficient sheaves have locally trivial relations
statement: Let C be a category with objects in universe u+1 and morphisms in universe u, essentially small in universe u+1, and J a Grothendieck topology. Let R be a Noetherian commutative ring in universe u+1. Assume sheafification for R-module-valued presheaves, that forgetting their module structure preserves sheaves, and that the maps inverted by sheafification are exactly locally bijective maps. Let F be a flat sheaf of R-modules. For any object U, finite family y_j in F(U) and finite matrix e_lj over R satisfying sum_j e_lj y_j=0 for every l, there is a covering sieve S of U such that along every f:V to U in S there exist finitely many sections z_m in F(V) and coefficients b_jm in R with y_j restricted to V = sum_m b_jm z_m and e b=0. Empty families and zero rings are allowed.

source.place: Tag 08FC, lemma-flat-eq, forward implication, specialized to a Noetherian constant coefficient ring

proof.text: For a finite matrix of constant coefficients, take finite generators of its kernel over the Noetherian coefficient ring. Tensor the resulting exact sequence of finite free constant module sheaves with the flat sheaf. Exactness is preserved. A section encoding the relation lies in the kernel, so local exactness of sheaves lifts it to the finite free generators on a covering sieve. The coordinates of that lift give the factorization matrix and sections. This is the proved source theorem CategoryTheory.Sheaf.hasLocallyTrivialRelations_of_flat; no new Lean declaration is introduced.
